sentence: Recent advances in meteorological modeling have been supported by the increasing availability of high-resolution reanalysis datasets and the development of machine learning techniques, both of which have become important for precipitation forecasting, as demonstrated by \citet{10512739}.

\citet{hersbach2020era5} introduced ERA5 with hourly coverage and a spatial resolution of approximately 31~km, showing marked improvements over ERA-Interim in reproducing variability and extremes across multiple atmospheric variables.
\citet{mcnicholl2021evaluating} found strong agreement between ERA5 near-surface air temperature and ground-based observations but also reported discrepancies under complex meteorological conditions.

\citet{doddy2021reanalysis} compared several reanalysis products for renewable energy applications in Ireland and showed that ERA5 generally outperforms MERRA-2 and JRA-55, while still exhibiting regional biases that require consideration.

For precipitation, \citet{lavers2022evaluation} evaluated 24-hour totals against 5,637 stations over 2001--2020, finding a general wet bias, lower annual maximum one-day amounts, and smaller random errors in winter than summer in the extratropics.

Although \citet{ridal2024cerra} reported improvements over ERA5 for several near-surface variables, the present study uses ERA5 for both predictors and target precipitation and does not assess whether CERRA would improve regional precipitation forecasting.}

Although \citet{ridal2024cerra} reported improvements over ERA5 for several near-surface variables, the present study uses ERA5 for both predictors and target precipitation and does not assess whether CERRA would improve regional precipitation forecasting.} \citet{palharini2021assessment} evaluated eleven satellite-based precipitation products across different regions of Brazil and found that no single product consistently captured extreme rainfall, with performance varying by region and event intensity.

Similarly, \citet{kumar2025long} evaluated CHIRPS and GSMaP\_ISRO rainfall estimates against gauge observations over India during 2000--2022 and found that GSMaP\_ISRO agreed more closely with station measurements than CHIRPS, while both products diverged notably over complex terrain such as the Western Ghats.

Among conventional machine-learning approaches, \citet{rahman2022rainfall} developed a fusion-based system for smart-city rainfall prediction that combines multiple classifiers with fuzzy logic, reporting improvements in prediction accuracy in their study.
\citet{adewoyin2021tru} proposed TRU-NET, which incorporates attention mechanisms and ERA5 inputs to produce high-resolution rainfall predictions over the UK.

At the global scale, \citet{singh2021deep} trained a residual U-Net on reanalysis data in a cubed-sphere framework and reported improved correlation skill over an operational numerical weather prediction system, while also emphasizing the need for hybrid integration and probabilistic evaluation.

\citet{miller2021analysis} examined short-term and seasonal rainfall forecasts in Kenya and found substantial regional differences in forecasting skill, highlighting the importance of localized validation.

More recently, \citet{latif2023assessing} compared statistical, machine-learning and deep-learning approaches to rainfall prediction and concluded that machine learning performed well across climates and timescales, with LSTM models among the most effective.

Where heavy precipitation was examined separately, aggregate results did not describe tail behaviour: TRU-NET underpredicted the largest daily amounts more than IFS \citep{adewoyin2021tru}, and \citet{otero2023intercomparison} compared architectures specifically with regard to extremes.

\citet{kendall2017uncertainties} introduced a probabilistic regression framework in which neural networks jointly predict the mean and variance of a Gaussian likelihood, allowing data-dependent uncertainty to be estimated directly from the model.

\citet{9001195} proposed a framework that combines assumed density filtering and Monte Carlo dropout to model both data and model uncertainty without retraining, reporting improvements in calibration and robustness across perception and control tasks.

\citet{klotz2022uncertainty} compared several probabilistic deep learning approaches for rainfall-runoff modeling and found that asymmetric Laplacian mixture networks produced more accurately calibrated predictions than Gaussian or dropout-based approaches, particularly under extreme flow conditions.

\citet{mena2021survey} reviewed a range of uncertainty estimation methods, including variational inference, Monte Carlo dropout, ensembles, and Dirichlet prior networks, and discussed their trade-offs in calibration, interpretability, and computational cost.
\citet{chakraborty2017interpretability} provided an early systematic overview of interpretability research, distinguishing model transparency, functionality, and different forms of explanation.

\citet{li2022interpretable} developed a unified taxonomy linking interpretation, interpretability, and trustworthiness, providing a general basis for evaluating explanations produced by machine learning systems.

\citet{vinuesa2021interpretable} discussed the role of interpretable deep learning in sustainable development and emphasized the value of models that incorporate meaningful and understandable representations.

\citet{temenos2023interpretable} developed an interpretable deep learning framework combining a compact CNN with SHAP-based explanations to provide both local and global feature attributions in remote-sensing classification.

\citet{yoganand2026shap} proposed a SHAP-integrated LeNet model with transfer learning for flood prediction in Telangana, combining engineered feature selection with attention-based convolutional layers and using SHAP to explain model outputs.

\citet{yang2024interpretable} reviewed recent developments in interpretable machine learning for weather and climate prediction, highlighting the use of feature attribution, attention mechanisms, and physics-informed approaches to examine relationships learned by data-driven models.

\citet{otero2023intercomparison} likewise used ERA5 predictors and precipitation fields for an architecture intercomparison, but their European daily contemporaneous modelling task differs from our six-hour-ahead hourly target.
Hourly precipitation observations at Dublin Airport were obtained from \citet{met_eireann_dublin_hourly}.

A related distinction is made by \citet{https://doi.org/10.1029/2026JH001291}, who treated ERA5-referenced precipitation evaluation as a model-consistency check and used satellite-derived IMERG as an independent observational benchmark.
As discussed by \citet{lerch2017forecaster}, evaluating forecasts only on cases selected by their observed outcomes can distort comparative rankings.

In subseasonal downscaling of weekly mean fields, \citet{goutham2023statistical} found that restricting the predictor domain to the predictand domain considerably degraded prediction quality, whereas shifting a predictand-sized domain westward did not improve on a centred one; this provides context rather than validation of six-hour precipitation prediction or of the present boxes.
